why: The case named in §3.1's corollary: a card resting on page ground with a --bg-soft hover. Cards are --bg-soft. It also carries .albumCover (a Spotify cover image), so on the studio-album grid — which sits in .section, i.e. bare --bg — it is a photograph on bare ground, which §3.2 forbids. Risk: the same class is reused by .pairGrid inside .altSection (background: --bg-soft, line 178), where the cell will now match its band; the 2px --line seam bed still draws the grid there, and the hover at 236 now lifts in both contexts instead of vanishing into the band.

The homepage catalogue is the same component one step low: cover art on a card painted page-ground, inside .section, which has no background of its own (page.module.css:55) — so the covers sit directly on --bg.

The mobile half of the same album card — cover art (.albumCover, line 249) on a cell painted page-ground on a --bg page. Desktop and mobile are separate components; fixing only one leaves the phone with the defect. No hover exists on touch, so this is the rest step alone; the 1px --rule seam bed still draws the grid.
